clue.text: The nubile Rebecca so favourably disposed?

definitions.meaning: in Genesis the marriageable Rebecca is met by Abraham's servant beside the well, so she was positioned at the well
situated advantageously, in a good position

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading needs the Bible story: Rebecca, of age to marry, was found at the well and so became Isaac's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated advantageously is said to be in a good spot, which matches being favourably disposed in the old sense of arranged.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of one taking blows in outback

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: the word out with its back letter brought round to the front
a handkerchief is what takes the blows when you blow your nose

explanation.surface: A thank-you to someone who has taken a beating in the Australian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outback' is not the Australian interior: the indicator is the word's own 'back', which brings OUT's final letter round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying thanks is the everyday way of acknowledging a kindness or a gift.

clue.text: Unknown priest writing up "George of the Circus"

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An anonymous cleric reviews a book about a circus performer called George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Circus' is John le Carré's nickname for the British secret service, where George Smiley works; 'up' reverses the whole string, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: George Smiley is the spymaster of le Carré's novels, based at the service headquarters known as the Circus.

clue.text: Sailor behind St Paul's

definitions.meaning: a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service was called by this bird name
Sir Christopher, the architect who designed St Paul's Cathedral in London

explanation.definitionFit: The bird name serves both for a woman in the Royal Navy and for the architect responsible for St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: All up with has-been: not as characters beyond recall

indicators.note: the letters are treated as loose characters to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the word as from has-been

explanation.surface: Everything is finished for a washed-up star who can no longer be remembered as a character.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and S from HASBEEN to leave HBEEN, then shuffle it with ALLUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing past saving is lost for good, which is what being past recovery or recall suggests.

clue.text: Prom performers duck out of this world

indicators.note: the word Prom is worked over, performed into a new shape
out signals that the letters come out of order

parts.note: the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: Musicians at a Promenade concert dodge leaving the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are London's summer concert season; 'out of this world' tempts as a phrase meaning wonderful, but 'out' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal can mean worldly or secular, belonging to this life rather than the spiritual one.

clue.text: Having constant inflammatory condition? Get stuffed!

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant
gout inflames the joints

explanation.surface: Someone with chronic gout is told rudely to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stuffed!' reads as a rude brush-off but is the definition taken literally: eat too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge yourself on food is to eat until you are stuffed.

clue.text: Tramp reaching end of road in song

definitions.text: Tramp reaching end of road in song

parts.words: Tramp reaching end of road in song
parts.note: the Rodgers and Hart song says she is a tramp, so the tramp in the song ends up being a woman of rank

explanation.walkthrough: The song is 'The ___ Is a Tramp'; there is also the Disney film pairing her with the Tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title identifies the tramp with a well-born woman.

clue.text: Short-termist's record hour no mere accident

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: by accident the letters fall in a different order

explanation.surface: A careless person keeps records of hours, and it was not a mere accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' rearranges NOMERE into EMERON.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a creature or thing that lasts only a day, so something living strictly for the short term.

clue.text: Natural cover of one held by care order

indicators.note: held by puts one piece inside the other
care is put in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wild ground cover for a child taken into council care under a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges CARE as ERCA, which then holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is the genus name of a low shrub that blankets moorland like a natural ground cover.

clue.text: Something from a lamb or a lion, roughly wrapped in pound note

indicators.note: wrapped in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: L stands for a pound (libra)

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are handled loosely and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something taken from a lamb or a lion, carelessly wrapped up in a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' turns A LION into ANOLI, which sits between L and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Wool grease extracted from sheep's fleece is a product that comes from lambs.

clue.text: Sound delightful? You utter poser!

indicators.note: utter here means say out loud, so the word before it is heard rather than read

parts.note: the word you, spoken, gives the opening sound of the answer
a poser is a fake, a phony

explanation.surface: A taunt: you sound delightful, you absolute fraud!
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like the intensifier in 'You utter phony!' but is the sound signal; the whole insult spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pleasantness of sound, a delightful harmony of tones.

clue.text: Off-road vehicles here in reserve?

definitions.meaning: a roadside pull-in where cars stop off the carriageway
to put by or set aside for later, as savings

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a British roadside stopping place, and the verb phrase means to set aside for the future.

clue.text: Anglo-American takes the rap sadly for Middle Eastern banker

indicators.note: takes means one piece holds the other

parts.note: E stands for English, as in Anglo

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Anglo-American takes the blame unhappily for a Middle Eastern financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges THE RAP. 'banker' is crossword shorthand for a river, something with banks, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker in crosswords is a river, and this great river flows through Iraq in the Middle East.

clue.text: Tautological observer?

parts.note: both halves of the compound mean a person who sees, so the name repeats itself

explanation.walkthrough: An eye sees and a witness sees, so the word says the same thing twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saw an event at first hand is an observer, and the word doubles up on that idea.

clue.text: Ignatius's new revelation giving one strength

indicators.note: a revelation shows the letters in a new arrangement

parts.note: the name with its possessive S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Saint Ignatius has a fresh vision that fortifies him.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive S is a real letter in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps you going nourishes and fortifies you, giving strength.

clue.text: We addicts very critical abusers? Not a trip!

indicators.note: not says letters are taken away from the rearranged fodder

parts.note: a year is one trip round the sun

explanation.surface: We solvers are harsh critics who abuse things, though we are not hallucinating.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of YEAR from VERY CRITICAL ABUSERS and rearrange the rest; 'abusers' doubles as a hint that the fodder is abused.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword solvers, the setter and readers of this puzzle, are devotees of crosswords.

clue.text: As is right and proper at home ground

parts.note: in means at home
a ground is a reason, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.definitionFit: Within sensible limits, which is the idiom for what is reasonable and right.

clue.text: Contractions from bearing? Yes, lots! Awful!

parts.note: S is the compass bearing south

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters are rearranged badly

explanation.surface: A woman in labour asks whether the contractions are many: yes, lots, and awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges YESLOTS into YSTOLES. 'bearing' tempts as childbearing.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the contractions of the heart muscle as it pumps blood.

clue.text: Establish counterblast, as it were?

parts.note: read the word as counter (deter) plus blast (mine)
read the word as counter (deter) plus blast (mine)

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'counterblast' into counter, meaning to deter, and blast, a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain or settle something is to establish it.

clue.text: See 21 across
Male impersonator with style? One valet disagrees

annotationWithheld.why: Male impersonator with style? One valet disagrees (5,6), VESTA TILLEY: the definition is Male impersonator, but no parse of 'with style? One valet disagrees' giving VESTA TILLEY could be found or confirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Male impersonator with style? One valet disagrees

clue.text: Drive an American chariot to some adoring Indians

parts.note: vim is drive or energy

explanation.surface: Push an American car in front of worshipping Indians.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hindu myth this is a flying chariot of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Sanskrit epics the gods ride in a flying chariot of this name.

clue.text: Restore memory of English king impressed by the navy

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into the navy, so these letters go inside

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: An English king forced into naval service learns again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' recalls the press gang that forced men into the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something again is to bring it back into memory.

clue.text: Dawn's fingers so promising?

definitions.meaning: Homer's stock epithet calls dawn pink-fingered
hopeful, looking good for the future

explanation.definitionFit: The colour word describes Homer's dawn and also means hopeful about prospects.

clue.text: Travesty of light o' love with knight

parts.note: a lamp is a light
the shortened of gives O
love is zero, O
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A mockery of a courtly romance with a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light o' love' looks like a flirt but splits into LAMP, O and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A satire or mocking caricature is a travesty of its subject.

clue.text: Nothing for charity?

definitions.meaning: the King James Bible's charity in Corinthians is rendered as this word in modern versions

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a score of zero and is also the modern rendering of charity in St Paul's letter.

clue.text: Sheep never-never left to shepherd

indicators.note: left means these letters have departed from the word

parts.note: the never-never is British slang for hire purchase, HP

explanation.surface: Sheep in the Australian outback are left for someone to look after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-never' suggests the Australian outback, but it is hire purchase, HP; take H and P from SHEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd something is to take charge of it and attend to it.

clue.text: After which one's in the majority

definitions.text: After which one's in the majority

parts.words: After which one's in the majority
parts.note: the legal age of majority in Britain is eighteen, so once past this birthday one is an adult

explanation.walkthrough: 'majority' is not the larger group but legal adulthood, reached at eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching the year after this age means coming of age legally.
